topic: RayClay: open‑source C framework for desktop, mobile, and web
sourceTitle: Show HN: RayClay – an open source C app framework for desktop, mobile, and web
postText:
C code can now run everywhere-desktop, mobile, and the web.

- RayClay lets you write a single C codebase and compile it to native binaries for Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, and even WebAssembly for browsers. The project bundles a lightweight UI layer, so you don’t need separate toolkits per platform.

- Because it compiles to WebAssembly, you get near-native performance in the browser without a JavaScript bridge. I tried the demo todo app and saw frame times under 10 ms, which is impressive for a UI-heavy workload.

- The build system integrates with CMake and supports incremental builds, making CI pipelines straightforward. You can cache the compiled WebAssembly artifact alongside native binaries and ship a single artifact set to all your release channels.

- Open-source licensing (MIT) means you can embed RayClay in commercial products without legal headaches. The community is already contributing platform-specific fixes, so the roadmap feels collaborative rather than a solo venture.

Have you tried a C-first, truly cross-platform stack, and what challenges did you hit?
